evidence.note: Signing certificate expired a day before the validation time, yet the signature still verifies against the configured cert. This is why logins keep working.

output.fix: The response validates, but the SP is trusting an expired signing key. Rotate the IdP signing certificate: generate a new one in the IdP, publish updated metadata, and install the new cert on the SP before the IdP starts using it. Use RSA-2048 or larger with SHA-256. Then set the SP to reject expired signing certificates, and add expiry monitoring or alerting on the IdP cert. Do not work around this by skipping signature or validity checks.

alternatives.why_not: The certificate is expired, but the SP currently accepts it and every other check passes, so there is no functional failure. The validator reports this as a posture issue (works, unsafe). It would become the cause if the SP enforced cert expiry.
